item.research_question: How can high-entropy alloys be designed to achieve simultaneous high damping capacity, high strength, and high ductility at elevated temperatures via Snoek relaxation?
item.material_system: Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi base HEA, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 (O-2 HEA), and (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98N2 (N-2 HEA)
item.processing_route: Arc-melting of pure metals (purity >99.9 wt%), TiN, and TiO2 in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere; remelted at least eight times; drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold (10 mm x 10 mm x 60 mm)
item.test_conditions: Damping: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0 Hz, 300 to 1100 K, heating rate 2 K min−1, strain amplitude 2 × 10−4; Mechanical: Room temperature, strain rate 1 × 10−3 s−1
key_findings: The O-2 and N-2 HEAs achieved a maximum damping capacity (tanδmax) of 0.020 and 0.027, respectively, at 1.0 Hz.
The damping peak temperature reached up to 800 K, with operating ranges of 60 K, 53 K, and 30 K for the base, O-2, and N-2 HEAs at 1.0 Hz.
The N-2 HEA exhibited a tensile yield strength of 1362 MPa, while the O-2 HEA reached 1138 MPa.
The O-2 HEA displayed a ductility of ~20%, which was double that of the base HEA (~10.8%).
Activation energies for interstitial reorientation were estimated at 2.06 eV (base), 2.40 eV (O-2), and 4.06 eV (N-2).
Approximately 18.5% of oxygen atoms in the O-2 HEA formed ordered oxygen complexes, whereas only ~5.3% of nitrogen atoms in the N-2 HEA formed ordered nitrogen complexes.
The base HEA showed a yield strength of ~810 MPa and a damping capacity of 0.014 at 1.0 Hz.
item.mechanism: The high damping capacity originates from Snoek-type relaxation caused by stress-induced position switches of interstitial atoms (oxygen or nitrogen) in the severely distorted bcc lattice. The high strength and ductility are attributed to solid-solution strengthening and ordered interstitial complexes-mediated strain hardening, where the complexes impede dislocation motion and enhance work hardening.
item.limitations: The text notes that the complexity of the alloy composition makes it difficult to conduct a complete peak deconvolution analysis based on all possible individual relaxation processes, and the specific clusters attributing to peaks in the base HEA could not be determined.
item.future_work: The authors state that the current alloy design strategy could be used to develop other high-damping HEAs as well.
quotes: Via Snoek relaxation and ordered interstitial complexes mediated strain hardening, the damping capacity of these HEAs is as high as 0.030
The addition of either oxygen or nitrogen to the base HEA did not appreciably deteriorate the work hardening behavior.
Atomic position switches of interstitials in these matrices are impeded by the high atomic-scale distortion fields.
